steps: Draw a steep hill rising to a high point on the left and sloping down to a valley.
Draw the next hill rising from the valley on the right.
Show the cyclist at the top of the first hill and the downhill path toward the next hill.
items.finalAnswer: A cyclist at the top of the first hill travelling downhill and then up the next hill.

Top of first hill                         Top of next hill
       High potential energy                    Potential energy increases
                ● Cyclist                                 ● Cyclist
               /   \                                     /   \

           ↓ Potential energy decreases   Kinetic energy is greatest
             Kinetic energy increases
steps: At the top of the first hill, the cyclist has gravitational potential energy due to height.
As the cyclist moves downhill, potential energy decreases and changes into kinetic energy; the cyclist’s speed increases.
At the bottom of the valley, kinetic energy is greatest and potential energy is least.
As the cyclist moves up the next hill, kinetic energy changes back into potential energy and the cyclist slows down.
If friction and air resistance are neglected, the cyclist can reach the same height on the next hill.
items.finalAnswer: Potential energy changes into kinetic energy on the way down, and kinetic energy changes back into potential energy on the way up.
